title: Erasmian Koine Greek alphabet — app clip pack
notes: Each clip is name then sound. Master file inserts 1.60s silence between clips for easy snipping. Cue times are for the master file. Two rows were regenerated later and are not in the master: they carry source, take and a note instead of master offsets. Each row carries a sha1 of its mp3, checked by tools/check_sounds.py, so a clip cannot be replaced without the record of what was spoken moving with it.

clips.note: chosen by ear over the clip cut from the old master and two other renderings, generated on its own rather than spliced — sound with a schwa — the voice cannot trill. NOTE: lesson 1 teaches rho TRILLED and this clip does not trill; the voice cannot, whether r is written once or three times. It is the best r available, and the lesson text and the clip now disagree on this one letter.

clips.name: Upsilon
clips.note: Fraser heard the NAME as "up silon" and asked for "oop silon": every other letter here opens on its own sound -- EP-silon, OM-icron, AY-ta -- and lesson 1 teaches upsilon as "u as in lute / put", cued oo. Standard English says UP-silon, so this was a teaching choice and not a correction. He then took the NAME from the shipped clip and only the SOUND from a new take, which is what this is: a splice, the method eta, ei and xi were repaired by. The sound was recorded in the sheet as "ew / ue", a value the cue guide had overruled long ago, so the record had been describing a sound the course does not teach. Cut in the silence either side with 10-30ms fades, re-spaced to lead 0.19 / gap 0.39 / tail 0.29 against pi's 0.16 / 0.35 / 0.26. The old clip peaked at -9.7 dB, louder than every other letter; this one is -13.6, where pi and epsilon sit. REOPENED AND RESTORED 2026-09-15. The lesson narration seemed to say OOP-silon, so the name was changed to match and this row said so for one commit. Fraser relistened to that narration block and it says UP-silon, as this clip and the whole vocabulary pack already did. Nothing needed changing. Judged by ear, Fraser.

clips.name: Phi

clips.name: Chi
clips.note: Both halves were rejected: the name came out with the soft ch of 'church' instead of /kaI/, and the sound came out as the WORD 'Bach'. Recued 'Kai.  Khh.' in one take, sound half lifted 5 dB. This clip settles what chi is: its sound measures 260 ms of sustained energy at zero-crossing 0.22-0.28, which is frication, not the burst-plus-tail of an aspirated stop. So it is the loch sound lesson 1 teaches, and chi stays a declared departure from Black's 'chemist'. Judged by ear, Fraser.

clips.name: Psi
clips.note: Atlas will say the NAME psi with its p, and will not say the bare cluster: English has no word-initial /ps/, so there is nothing in the voice's experience to produce. The second half is therefore not spoken at all — it is the first 160 ms of this clip's own name, cut at the vowel and faded. Splicing from the deck's psuche was tried first and failed: that clip has NO plosive release, energy climbing smoothly out of silence into frication, so there was never a /p/ in it to lift. Fraser heard that before it was measured. Judged by ear, Fraser.

clips.name: epsilon + iota
clips.note: The same fault and the same fix as 07_eta: cued 'ay', said 'eye', where Black gives eight. One cue settled both. Judged by ear, Fraser.

clips.name: omicron + upsilon
clips.note: 'oo' was read as letters. 'ooh' gives Black's soup vowel. Judged by ear, Fraser.
